title: What Conda and Miniconda Are
description: Conda is a package and environment manager that creates isolated Python environments — each with its own Python version and libraries — so projects never conflict. Miniconda is the minimal installer (conda + Python, ~200 MB); Anaconda adds 150+ preinstalled science packages (~3 GB). For AI work, Miniconda is the standard: install small, add only what each project needs.

demo.program:
print("Conda: isolated Python envs (own Python + libs per project, no conflicts).")
print("Miniconda: conda + Python, ~200MB. THE installer for AI work.")
print("Anaconda: +150 science packages, ~3GB. Heavier, rarely needed now.")
print("Install small, add per project: Miniconda.")

t: Environments: The Isolation That Saves Projects
title: Environments: The Isolation That Saves Projects
description: Each conda environment is a separate Python universe: project A can use torch 2.0 on Python 3.10 while project B uses torch 2.3 on Python 3.11, with zero interference. Create with 'conda create -n myenv python=3.11', activate with 'conda activate myenv'. The base environment stays pristine — never install project packages into base.

demo.program:
print("conda create -n projA python=3.10  # torch 2.0 universe")
print("conda create -n projB python=3.11  # torch 2.3 universe")
print("Zero interference. Base stays PRISTINE: never install project pkgs in base.")

title: Essential Conda Commands
description: The daily commands: 'conda create -n NAME python=X.Y', 'conda activate NAME', 'conda install PACKAGE', 'conda list', 'conda env list', 'conda deactivate', 'conda remove -n NAME --all'. For AI: install pytorch with the cuda channel spec from pytorch.org's command generator — copy the exact command, because CUDA builds differ by version.

demo.program:
cmds = ["conda create -n ai python=3.11", "conda activate ai", "conda install numpy",
        "conda list", "conda env list", "conda deactivate"]
for c in cmds:
    print(f"  $ {c}")
print("PyTorch: copy the EXACT command from pytorch.org (CUDA builds differ).")

title: Channels: conda-forge and Priority
description: Channels are package sources: 'defaults' (Anaconda's) and 'conda-forge' (community, usually fresher). For AI work, conda-forge first is the common setup — newer builds of numpy, scipy, and friends. Set with 'conda config --add channels conda-forge' and strict priority to avoid mixed-channel conflicts. Channel conflicts cause the mysterious solver hangs; strict priority prevents them.

demo.program:
print("defaults: Anaconda's. conda-forge: community, fresher (AI standard).")
print("conda config --add channels conda-forge")
print("conda config --set channel_priority strict")
print("Strict priority: prevents mixed-channel solver hangs.")

title: environment.yml: Reproducible Environments
description: environment.yml declares an environment — name, channels, dependencies — and 'conda env create -f environment.yml' rebuilds it exactly anywhere. Commit it to git per project: the environment becomes versioned documentation. Export with 'conda env export > environment.yml' (use --from-history for the clean human-readable version listing only what you asked for).

demo.program:
print("environment.yml: name + channels + deps -> conda env create -f environment.yml")
print("Commit per project: environment as versioned documentation.")
print("Export: conda env export --from-history (clean: only what YOU asked for).")

title: Conda + pip: The Peaceful Coexistence
description: Some AI packages exist only on PyPI — the rule is conda first, pip second, pip only after all conda installs, and never conda-after-pip in the same env (it breaks the solver's model). Install conda packages, then 'pip install' the rest. For heavy pip needs, consider pip-only venvs instead — but for CUDA-adjacent AI work, conda's binary packaging wins.

demo.program:
print("Order: conda installs FIRST, pip SECOND, never conda-after-pip.")
print("Some packages are PyPI-only: that's what the pip step is for.")
print("CUDA-adjacent AI: conda binaries win. Pure-Python: venv also fine.")

title: Use Case: PyTorch GPU Environment
description: The standard AI env: 'conda create -n torch python=3.11', activate, then the pytorch.org conda command for your CUDA version (e.g., pytorch, torchvision, torchaudio, pytorch-cuda=12.1 from pytorch + nvidia channels). Verify with 'python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())"' — True means the GPU is live. Export the yml immediately while it works.

demo.program:
print("conda create -n torch python=3.11 && conda activate torch")
print("# then the pytorch.org conda command for YOUR cuda version")
print('python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())"  # True = GPU live')
print("Export environment.yml IMMEDIATELY while it works.")

t: Use Case: One Env Per Project
title: Use Case: One Env Per Project
description: The discipline: every project gets its own environment named for the project, with its own yml in the repo. Project ends? The env documents exactly what it needed. New machine? 'conda env create' per repo. Environments are cheap (disk) and conflicts are expensive (days) — the math favors many envs.

demo.program:
print("Per project: conda create -n <project> + environment.yml IN the repo.")
print("Envs are cheap (disk). Conflicts are expensive (days).")
print("Math favors many envs: one per project, always.")

title: Mamba: The Fast Solver
description: Mamba is a drop-in faster conda solver (same commands, 'mamba' instead of 'conda') that resolves dependencies in seconds where conda takes minutes. Install via 'conda install mamba -n base -c conda-forge', then use mamba for installs. For AI envs with huge dependency trees, mamba turns coffee-break solves into instant ones. Micromamba is the static-binary variant for containers.

demo.program:
print("conda install mamba -n base -c conda-forge")
print("Then: mamba install ... (same commands, seconds not minutes).")
print("AI dep trees are huge: mamba = coffee-break -> instant.")
print("Micromamba: static binary for containers.")

title: Cleaning: Reclaiming Conda Disk Space
description: Conda hoards: package caches, unused tarballs, and old envs eat tens of GB. 'conda clean --all' purges caches (answer yes), 'conda env list' + remove dead envs, and check pkgs/ size periodically. A fresh Miniconda is 200 MB; a year-old one can be 30 GB — the difference is all cache and corpses. Clean quarterly.

demo.program:
print("conda clean --all  (purge caches: the GB eater)")
print("Remove dead envs: conda remove -n old --all")
print("Fresh: 200MB. Year-old: 30GB (cache + corpses). Clean QUARTERLY.")

t: Conda vs venv vs Docker: Choosing Isolation
title: Conda vs venv vs Docker: Choosing Isolation
description: venv: lightweight, Python-only, no binary deps — fine for pure-Python tools. Conda: Python + binary stack (CUDA, MKL) — the AI default. Docker: whole OS-level isolation — the deployment/sharing answer. Ladder: venv for scripts, conda for AI dev, Docker for shipping. Many AI devs use conda INSIDE Docker for the best of both.

demo.program:
print("venv  : light, Python-only. Scripts + pure-Python tools.")
print("conda : Python + binaries (CUDA/MKL). THE AI dev default.")
print("docker: OS-level. Shipping + sharing.")
print("Ladder: venv < conda < docker. Many use conda INSIDE docker.")

title: Troubleshooting: Solver Hangs and Conflicts
description: The fixes: use mamba (kills most hangs), strict channel priority (kills conflicts), install big things together in one command (solver sees the whole picture), and when truly stuck, export --from-history, delete the env, recreate fresh. Never 'conda install' repeatedly hoping — each attempt constrains the solver further. Fresh envs are cheap; fighting solvers is not.

demo.program:
print("Hang: mamba. Conflicts: strict priority. Big installs: ONE command together.")
print("Truly stuck: export --from-history, delete env, recreate fresh.")
print("Fresh envs cheap; solver fights expensive. Don't install-and-hope repeatedly.")

title: Pinning Python and CUDA Versions
description: AI reproducibility needs pins: 'python=3.11' in create, 'pytorch-cuda=12.1' in install, and the yml records everything. CUDA version must match the NVIDIA driver (driver >= toolkit). The yml is the contract: same file, same env, same results. Unpinned envs drift with every solve — pinned envs are time machines.

demo.program:
print("Pin: python=3.11, pytorch-cuda=12.1, everything in yml.")
print("CUDA toolkit <= NVIDIA driver version. The yml = the contract.")
print("Unpinned: drifts every solve. Pinned: time machine.")

title: Base Environment Hygiene
description: Keep base minimal: conda, mamba, and nothing else. Every project package goes in its env. A polluted base (torch in base!) causes the classic 'works in base, breaks in env' confusion and slows every solve. If base is already polluted, reinstalling Miniconda fresh takes ten minutes — often faster than untangling.

print("Polluted base (torch in base!): 'works in base, breaks in env' confusion.")
print("Untangling vs 10-min fresh Miniconda reinstall: reinstall usually wins.")
